COMMANDER'S NARRATIVE SUMMARY

    On 8 August 1965 the Second Battalion returned to the United States at
San Diego, California. The majority of officers and men were transferred
to new commands. During September a Combined Fire Support Exercise was con-
ducted for military representatives of SEATO and this organization provided
the ground maneuver element. During early November 1965 a reinforced platoon
from "G" Company participated as aggressors for the U.S. Army Operation
TENDERTOUCH. During the middle of November 1965 this organization conducted
a PHIBLEX off the USS PRINCETON. Three rifle companies and elements of H&S
Company participated; however, companies were far below the manning level.
On 15 November 1965 the Regimental Landing Team-5 special training program
was implemented; however, due to personnel TAD to schools, commitments of
higher authority, and on board strength of approximately 50%, training was
very limited.

EVENT
The Third Battalion, Ninth Marines was redesignated the Second Battalion, Fifth Marines. Lieutenant Colonel C. E. MC PARTLIN, Jr., was the Commanding Officer.

The Battalion returned to the United States, arriving at San Diego, California.

Lieutenant Colonel C. E. MC PARTLIN, Jr., was relieved as Commanding Officer by Captain C. H. RAM. The following billets were filled on this date:

S-1: First Lieutenant T. BOYD
S-2: First Lieutenant E. A. KRATOVIL, Jr.
S-4: Captain H. T. WINSTON
CO, H&SCo: First Lieutenant P. C. ROLLINS
CO, "E"Co: First Lieutenant T. R. MINOR
CO, "F"Co: First Lieutenant D. G. WINTER
CO, "G"Co: First Lieutenant D. H. HERING
CO, "H"Co: First Lieutenant J. J. DOHERTY

Captain C. H. RAM was relieved as Commanding Officer by Major J. R. CATT. Captain C. H. RAM became the Executive Officer.

SEATO DEMONSTRATION
A combined fire support exercise was conducted by units of Regimental Landing Team Five for military representatives of the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization. The Battalion was the ground maneuver element.

Captain C. H. RAM was relieved as Executive Officer by Major T. E. BULGER. Captain C. H. RAM became the Commanding Officer, H&S Company.

Major J. R. CATT was relieved as Commanding Officer by Major L. W. T. WALLER, II. Major J. R. CATT became the S-3.

Major J. R. CATT was relieved as the S-3 by Major R. A. PAPE. Major J. R. CATT was transferred out of the Battalion.

Gunnery Sergeant J. J. SLOCUM was assigned as the S-2. First Lieutenant D. H. HERING was relieved as CO, "G" Company, by Captain R. E. GARRETT.

EVENT
First Lieutenant D. G. WINTER was relieved as CO, "F" Company by First Lieutenant G. S. BURGETT.

PARTICIPATED IN OPERATION TENDERTOUCH
The 1st Platoon (Rein), "G" Co, under the command of 2ndLt W. W. JEFFERY participated as aggressors in the U.S. Army Operation Tendertouch which was conducted by the 3rd Brigade, 5th Infantry Division (Mechanized), Fort Carson, Colorado, at Marine Corps Base, Camp Pendleton, California.

Captain C. H. RAM was relieved as CO, H&S Co, by Captain L. W. FAHRNI. Captain C. H. RAM was transferred out of the Battalion.

CONDUCTED PHIBLEX
The Battalion conducted a PHIBLEX which was a movement by helicopter from the USS PRINCETON to Marine Corps Base, Camp Pendleton, California. Three (3) rifle companies and elements of H&S Co. participated, however, companies were at approximately 40% manning level.

Captain R. E. GARRETT was relieved as CO, "G" Co, by Captain J. F. O'ROURKE. Captain R. E. GARRETT was transferred out of the Battalion.

Captain L. W. FAHRNI was relieved as CO, H&S Co, by Captain R. D. HUGHES.

Major T. E. BULGER was relieved as Executive Officer by Major R. A. PAPE. Major T. E. BULGER was transferred out of the Battalion. First Lieutenant T. BOYD was relieved as S-1 by First Lieutenant D. R. WEST. First Lieutenant T. R. MINOR was relieved as CO, "E" Co, by First Lieutenant D. E. MARCUM. First Lieutenant T. R. MINOR was transferred out of the Battalion. First Lieutenant G. S. BURGETT was relieved as CO, "F" Co, by Captain R. A. HICKETHIER.

Gunnery Sergeant J. J. SLOCUM was relieved as S-2 by Captain A. H. MOORE.

Major L. W. T. WALLER, II, was relieved as Commanding Officer by Lieutenant Colonel R. H. USKURAIT. Major L. W. T. WALLER, II, became the Executive Officer. Major R. A. PAPE became the S-3.
